Inventory supplied November 7: 2,268 unused science questions. This plan assigns 1530 and keeps 738 in reserve. Finishing the bank is not required; quality review and AAMC practice take priority.

November 9–20: 35 UWorld science questions per regular day. November 23–December 4: 45. December 7–January 7: alternate 50-question UWorld days with 40-question AAMC days, excluding exams, review and consolidation. January 8 onward: no new UWorld.

Every UWorld task specifies the exact subject, subtype and count. Build separate Unused sets for each listed subtype. If the platform includes extra questions to preserve a passage, finish that passage and subtract the extra from the next assignment of the same subtype.
The counts are a plan, not live UWorld syncing. If you have already used questions since this inventory, reduce the corresponding assignment rather than repeating it as unseen.

If you miss a day or cannot finish review, resume the unfinished assignment before the next one. Do not double the following day. Reserve questions replace other new questions when a full length reveals a weakness; they are not extra homework.
Times are focused study time; take 5–10 minute breaks between blocks and a meal break. A 330-minute study day takes longer than 5.5 hours on the clock.
Question counts are targets, not quotas. If review takes longer, reduce new questions and use that time for review. Do not skip explanations to finish a count.
For each missed or guessed answer: identify the tested concept, locate passage evidence, explain why your choice fails, and write one prevention rule. Make only 1–2 short cards for reusable gaps.
C/P: write the governing relationship and units before calculating. Practice rearranging equations and estimating without a calculator.
Early practice: untimed and untutored, reviewing after each small set. Use tutored mode when learning a new topic. Later timed blocks: no notes, hints or answer checking.
Anki: prioritize due cards and missed-question concepts. Cap work at the scheduled time; reduce new cards if reviews become unmanageable.

Each Sunday checkpoint: compare similar unused sets, identify the three most repeated errors and replace next week’s repair topics with those weaknesses. UWorld percentages are not MCAT score conversions.
If a day is missed, resume today and move only the most important unfinished repair task into the next catch-up slot. Never double the next day automatically.
Full-lengths replace the normal daily checklist and require about 7.5 hours including breaks. Use unused scored exams when possible. Record section scores and whether an exam was repeated.
After each full-length, reassess the January exam using the recent timed score trend. A 510 remains the stretch target; 502–505 is an intermediate goal, not a guarantee.

pankow_guide: Use your existing MrPankow deck; do not reimport, reset or resuspend learned cards. The calendar does not change Anki automatically.

In Anki Browse, choose the relevant topic tag or subdeck in your own deck, then narrow to is:new is:suspended. Preview the results and use Toggle Suspend only on the small batch you want to learn. Tag names differ by deck version; the schedule supplies topic names, not invented exact tags.

Begin with at most 25 new cards per eligible day for five study days, then aim for 40 if due reviews fit. A ceiling is not a quota. No scheduled new cards on full-length, exam-review, weekly catch-up or final consolidation days.
Complete due reviews first. Say the meaning in your own words and give a fresh example before rating a card. A familiar-looking term is not enough if you cannot apply it.
If due reviews take more than the allocated time, stop adding new cards. If needed, use your next catch-up block for the backlog and reduce question volume temporarily, not question review quality.

Each calendar topic is a suggested window. If a section exceeds the daily new-card cap, continue it the next day and move later topics forward. If it is already learned, review due cards and move to the next unfinished topic.
Use 45 minutes of the normal 60-minute Anki block for MrPankow and 15 for science mistakes. P/S application questions remain scheduled; videos are optional explanations for stubborn concepts.

Weekly: count remaining unseen cards and divide by remaining eligible new-card days through January 7. If that pace is too high, prioritize weak concepts rather than assuming the whole deck must be finished. Exact completion cannot be predicted without your remaining card count.
For a well-established concept, skip its video. For a shaky definition or example, use the exact optional video title beside the day’s topic, then return to cards and questions.
